R008-01.notes: P2 raises 'dishonest' charge; P3-4 explain the ruins' function. A overreaches, B is only P1 detail, D contradicts author's partial approval in P5.

flags: minor: near-verbatim lift of P1's last sentence; pure locate-and-match detail item
R008-02.notes: P1: 'Builders were sometimes instructed to leave stones scattered at the base.' Others unsupported.

R008-03.notes: Souvenir analogy voices the modern 'feeling without the thing' objection; P3 opens 'But that judgment assumes...' C is the trap (author doesn't think them worthless). A literalizes the analogy.

flags: minor: correct choice paraphrases the immediately preceding sentence ('little evidence that they were [trying to deceive]'), making it very direct
R008-04.notes: Guidebooks openly said ruins were new -> no intent to deceive. C contradicts 'owners were often proud'.

R008-05.notes: 'an occasion for a particular state of mind' = opportunity. A 'celebration' is the common-meaning trap; C 'excuse' plausible but carries a pejorative sense not intended.

flags: minor: correct choice A echoes the key word ('furnished') and the preceding sentence on contemplating decay; B and C are literal-furniture distractors that few will pick, so effectively a two-option item with D
minor: substantial overlap with R008-07 — both keys are 'reflection on time/decay/impermanence'; answering one gives away the other
R008-06.notes: Previous sentence: pleasure of contemplating decay; ruin as fixture that sets the scene for reflection. D (wealth) is the only real competitor, unsupported in P3-4.

flags: minor: key nearly duplicates R008-06's key (reflection on time and impermanence); consider differentiating the skill tested
R008-07.notes: P4: history as a mood, present 'both important and fleeting'; 'did not need to be old... needed only to be broken.' A contradicts P3; B contradicts 'not primarily a record to be consulted'.

flags: minor: correct choice A is the longest and the only two-part 'approving..., while noting...' answer — a common test-wise tell
R008-08.notes: 'in some ways we are right to... has saved a great deal' = approval; 'Yet the impulse... has not disappeared' = persistence. B misreads; D ignores evaluative 'right to'.

R008-09.notes: 'Yet the impulse behind the sham ruin has not disappeared. It survives whenever...' A is the trap (barn wood isn't original materials preservation); C contradicts the non-deception theme.

flags: minor: C is the only choice that maps onto all five paragraphs, and A/D are easily eliminated; overlaps conceptually with R008-01 (both reward the 'objection then rebuttal' reading)
R008-10.notes: P1 describes, P2 objection, P3-4 rebut, P5 links to present. B has no two rival theories; A not a history survey; D contradicts P5.
